raw_text:
Independent review of run r-20261008T005712906522-jtfm-token-error-labels (plan
imas-ambix:jt60sa-facility-mint section 16), read at its head
9e5aac3699e124fa61b0364e2e1becf85f5d7886 on base 735f1be0f3d3e417b1f1cf5d7fe0562d4fdee55a.
The node is the section-16 repair the followup "Resume after the fleet move" names: read_channel
labelled its not-cached and half-written errors through the review's own strict token.

VERDICT goal: section 16's repair is that read_channel's error labels do not route through the
strict pulse-token grammar, plus a CLI-level refusal test. It is met. read_channel
(packages/imas-alambic/src/imas_alambic/eddb.py:320, :330) now names the channel through a new
non-refusing _channel_label (eddb.py:121) in both cache-fault messages -- 4 passed (EXIT=0) and
a full packages/imas-alambic/tests run 57 passed (EXIT=0) in my own worktree, against the
repository's shared project environment.

VERDICT done_when: the dispatched measure is this record stored parsed with all six dimensions,
which this record satisfies. The node's own done-when is that a bare integer read that misses the
cache, or finds a half-written channel, names the cache fault instead of "101154 is not an EDDB
pulse token", and that eddb_token still refuses a bare digit. tests/test_eddb_read_errors.py:35
("channel 101154/MMSYS/CS1 is not cached at") and :52 ("... is half-written") pin both bare-digit
messages; :66 pins the unchanged lettered message "channel E101154/MMSYS/CS1 is not cached at";
:74 pins that eddb_token(101154) still raises with "series letter". The CLI refusal is pinned at
test_cli.py:52. Both arms of the gate carry the same 14 failure ids, so zero added.

VERDICT write_paths: the node's declared fence was eddb.py, the two new/extended test files and the
evidence fragment; the single commit's diff touches exactly those four paths and nothing else
(git show --stat: eddb.py +18/-2, test_cli.py +38, new test_eddb_read_errors.py +75, fragment +14).

VERDICT manifest: read; it records the head arm of packages/imas-alambic/tests tests/data/test_eddb_cache.py
at 14 failed / 75 passed (EXIT=1) against a base arm of 14 failed / 70 passed (EXIT=1), whole-tree
ruff EXIT=0, and a negative control that reverts read_channel to eddb_token.

VERDICT diff: one commit, parent 735f1be0, so the reviewed diff is exactly this change. _channel_label
returns eddb_token's canonical form for a series-lettered token and str(int(digits)) for a bare
integer, the same directory name normalised_shot yields, so no message names a directory that does
not exist.

REPRODUCTION (independent, in my own tree). The head is not an ancestor of my checkout, so I
extracted 9e5aac36 with git archive into a scratch tree and ran the focused gate:
`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/imas-ambix/.venv PYTHONPATH=<scratch>/packages/imas-alambic/src
uv run --no-sync pytest -q packages/imas-alambic/tests/test_eddb_read_errors.py` -> 4 passed,
EXIT=0; and the whole directory `packages/imas-alambic/tests` -> 57 passed, EXIT=0. I then applied
the node's own mutation (sed 's/_channel_label(shot)/eddb_token(shot)/g' on eddb.py, reverting both
read_channel labels (so both sites use eddb_token)): the two bare-digit tests failed with
"101154 is not an EDDB pulse token; name the pulse with its series letter and digits, for example
E101154" -- 2 failed, 2 passed, EXIT=1 -- and the two lettered/strict tests stayed green, which is
the correct discrimination. The guard is therefore load-bearing, not a test that passes vacuously.

ADDED FAILURES. Derived from the reviewed run's own gate logs, not from this review's runs.
gate-base.log header revision 735f1be0, tail "14 failed, 70 passed", EXIT=1; gate-head.log header
revision 9e5aac36, tail "14 failed, 75 passed", EXIT=1. The 14 FAILED ids are set-identical between
the two arms (comm -13 and comm -23 both empty), all in tests/data/test_eddb_cache.py, so
added_failure_count=0 and added_failure_ids=[]. The 5 newly-passing tests are the node's own.

SCORES (0..20): goal_fidelity 20, done_when 20, scope_discipline 20, fit 20, reuse 20,
evidence 19, durability 19; total 118. evidence keeps one point because the base arm's second
header line prints an empty full-sha field (the short sha 735f1be0 is on the header line and the
manifest carries the full revision, so this is cosmetic) and because the negative control is the
node's own claim which I re-derived rather than read. durability keeps one point because no test
covers _channel_label's leading-zero normalisation for a bare token (str(int("0101154")) is not
pinned), a minor but real coverage gap. ruff check over the three changed Python files exits 0; the
naming scans are clean (E101154/E900001/CS1 are EDDB pulse tokens and a channel name, not plan
labels); the commit body is present and carries no AI trailer.

BEFORE/AFTER, representative. At base, `read_channel(root, 101154, "MMSYS", "CS1")` on a miss raised
EddbCacheError "101154 is not an EDDB pulse token; name the pulse with its series letter and digits,
for example E101154" -- the remote-address grammar's refusal, misdescribing a cache miss. At head
the same call raises "channel 101154/MMSYS/CS1 is not cached at <path>". A lettered read is
unchanged: read_channel(root, "E101154", ...) still says "channel E101154/MMSYS/CS1 is not cached at".
eddb_token(101154) still refuses, so the remote address grammar is untouched.

FOLLOW-ON (carried from the node, not introduced by it): tests/data/test_eddb_cache.py holds 14
failures present identically at base and head, from the token-strictness commit that made
write_channel/eddb_token refuse a letterless shot while those fixtures still pass bare-digit shots.
Repairing those fixtures or the write path is outside this node's scope.
